_meta.purpose: An evidence-gated hyper-edge corpus answering one question: what do females need? Each edge joins a NEED node to a POPULATION node and a LEVER node, and carries the eight gates this tree already uses for evidence (TIER, GROUND, DENOM, UNIVERSE, QUORUM, BLIND, TRUNC, PROVENANCE).
_meta.epistemic_status: This corpus records WHAT PUBLISHED SOURCES SAY. It is not a clinical instrument, not a needs assessment, and not a validation of any program. No claim here was measured on a patient by this author. The population focus is women in, or returning from, behavioural-health and justice systems, because that is the population this project serves; the general-population claims are labelled GENERAL and kept separate so a reader cannot mistake one universe for the other.
what_this_cannot_tell_you: Whether a specific local provider delivers any of these levers.
Prevalence in Berks County, PA, or in any single facility: every prevalence figure here is national or from the named study's own setting.
Whether an intervention WORKS. Most edges record that a need exists and that a guidance body names a lever; effect sizes are out of scope and would need their own corpus.
Anything from a woman who was not already inside a study, a survey, or a review.
_meta.gate_vocabulary_source: ARC/cain/hyper_edge_dreams.json (states NO_QUORUM | BLIND | CUT) and MANDATES.md TIER/GROUND/DENOM/UNIVERSE rules.

states.VERIFIED: tier A or B, a quotation retrieved from the cited source, and (for prevalence claims) a denominator.
states.LEAD: real but under-powered here: tier C or D, single-source, unstated denominator, or a summary of a summary. Never upgraded without a second independent source.
states.BLIND: the source could not be retrieved, so the claim is recorded as unanswered rather than guessed.
states.CUT: retrieved and rejected. Kept in the file so the rejection is auditable and cannot be silently re-derived.

_meta.counts_note: Derived, never typed: tools/validate_female_needs_corpus.py recomputes every field here and fails when this block disagrees with the data. The first draft carried edges=20, sources=15, verified=17, lead=3 against a file holding 22, 18, 13 and 9 -- hand-kept count blocks drift silently, which is why the validator owns them.

needs.label: Safety from retraumatisation, not just the absence of an incident

module.title: What safety actually means in a care setting
objectives: Distinguish trauma-informed from trauma-specific care
Name the six SAMHSA principles and where each shows up in a waiting room
Identify one retraumatising practice in a setting the learner knows
module.misconception: That safety means a locked door and a camera. Both are present in settings this corpus cites as retraumatising.

edges.claim: A trauma-informed programme must actively resist retraumatisation, not merely acknowledge trauma exists.
edges.intervention: Train every staff role, including front desk and security, on retraumatisation and give clients a route to report it.

ground.quote: responds by fully integrating knowledge about trauma into policies, procedures, and practices, while seeking to actively resist retraumatization

edges.denominator: n/a - guidance, not a prevalence claim
edges.universe: U.S. behavioural-health service settings, 2024 SAMHSA programme definition
edges.quorum: single authoritative body
edges.provenance: retrieved 2026-11-16 from the SAMHSA programme page; the page defines the approach, it does not measure compliance anywhere

edges.claim: Women in prison report PTSD at roughly three and a half times the rate men in prison do.
edges.intervention: Screen for trauma at intake and re-assess during custody, not once at the gate.

edges.denominator: 21% of women in prison vs 6% of men in prison
edges.universe: incarcerated U.S. population, national survey data as reported by CCJ 2024
edges.quorum: corroborated: S-WGIC reports 1 in 3 justice-involved women meeting PTSD criteria and 50% lifetime, same direction, different cut

corroboration.note: extracted with pdftotext -layout from the PDF at the cited URL on 2026-11-16; the brief is quoting Lynch et al. 2017, so this is a second-hand figure corroborating a tier-B assessment, not a primary measurement

edges.intervention: Adopt a validated women's instrument (WRNA, SPIn-W, or SRAG-R) rather than a male-normed tool.

edges.denominator: 15 of 41 participating state departments of corrections

answer.question: What do females need?
answer.one_line: Safety first, then a relationship that survives the transition; care that treats her as a mother and a body with its own clinical trajectory; product, money, childcare and a bed as clinical necessities; and a say in the design.

ranked.why: Everything else is retraumatising if this is absent; PTSD prevalence is 21% vs 6% among incarcerated men.
Two thirds carry a diagnosis; treating one half and waiting on the other loses her.
Children are the reason women cite for engaging and the reason they are refused a bed that takes them.
Earlier onset of serious harm means the same threshold is not the same care.
A material need with a measurable failure: 50% changing every 30 minutes on free pads.
Transport and childcare, not motivation, are the named employment barriers.
Policy exclusion, not affordability alone, closes the door.
Women can name the eight domains themselves; services that ask still reach only 15 of 137.

answer.ordering_note: The rank is an argument from the evidence's own logic (safety underlies the rest), NOT a measured effect ranking. No study here compared these eight against each other, and none should be read as saying need 5 is less urgent than need 2 for a particular woman.
